title: Heritage sites in Goa: churches, temples, forts and rock art
seo_title: Heritage Sites in Goa: Churches, Forts and Historical Places
meta_description: Heritage sites in Goa beyond the beaches: UNESCO churches of Old Goa, Tambdi Surla, Usgalimal rock carvings, Safa Masjid, forts and Fontainhas, with museums.
summary: Goa's one UNESCO World Heritage Site is the Churches and Convents of Goa (1986) at Old Goa, including the Basilica of Bom Jesus and the Se Cathedral. Older and less visited layers include the Usgalimal rock carvings, the Kadamba temple at Tambdi Surla, the Arvalem caves, the Safa Masjid at Ponda and a chain of coastal forts.

paras: Goa is often presented as a Portuguese place, but its history is much longer. Rock carvings at Usgalimal and stone tools along its rivers show people here long before farming. The region was later ruled by the Bhojas, the Chalukyas of Badami, the Shilaharas and, from about the 10th to 14th centuries, the Kadambas of Goa, whose capitals were Chandor (Chandrapur) and then Gopakapattana near today's Panaji. It passed to the Bahmani and then the Adil Shahi sultanates of Bijapur before the Portuguese captured the city of Goa in 1510.

Portuguese rule lasted until 1961, far longer than British rule in most of India. That long period shaped churches, houses, food, music and law, but it also moved temples inland, beyond the early Portuguese territory, and changed the map of where communities lived. A good heritage visit keeps all of these layers in view.

sections.h2: UNESCO World Heritage Site: the Churches and Convents of Goa
paras: Old Goa, upriver from Panaji on the Mandovi, was the capital of Portuguese Asia in the 16th and 17th centuries. Epidemics and silting led to its decline, and the government moved to Panaji in the 19th century. What remains is a group of large churches and convents in open ground, inscribed by UNESCO in 1986.

The Basilica of Bom Jesus (completed 1605) holds the tomb of St Francis Xavier, with a marble and jasper mausoleum made in Florence. The Se Cathedral, completed in the early 17th century, is one of the largest churches in Asia. The Church of St Francis of Assisi, the Chapel of St Catherine, the Church of St Cajetan, modelled on St Peter's in Rome, and the Church of Our Lady of the Rosary on the Holy Hill complete the group, and the tall ruined tower of St Augustine shows the scale of what has been lost. Our [heritage walk in Old Goa](heritage-walk-in-old-goa.html) guide covers the route on foot.

sections.h2: Ancient temples and archaeological sites in Goa
paras: The Mahadeva temple at Tambdi Surla, at the foot of the Western Ghats in the Bhagwan Mahavir sanctuary, is the best preserved Kadamba-period temple in Goa, usually dated to around the 12th to 13th centuries. It is built in basalt, and its remote site is often given as the reason it survived. The Arvalem caves near Sanquelim are a small group of rock-cut chambers, with dates debated between about the 6th and 7th centuries; local tradition links them to the Pandavas.

Usgalimal, on the bank of the Kushavati river in Sanguem taluka, has more than a hundred carvings on laterite, including animals, human figures and a labyrinth pattern, usually considered prehistoric. They were recorded only in the 1990s. Our session on [rock art of India](rock-art-of-india.html) explains how such carvings are dated and why the debates matter.

The main Hindu temples of central Goa, such as Shri Mangueshi, Shri Shantadurga and Shri Mahalsa around Ponda, were rebuilt in the 17th and 18th centuries after their deities were moved inland. Their lamp towers (deepastambhas) and mixed temple and colonial forms are a distinct Goan style. The Safa Masjid at Ponda, built in 1560 under the Adil Shahi sultans, has a large stepped tank.

The Portuguese built and rebuilt a ring of coastal forts. Fort Aguada (early 17th century) guarded the Mandovi and had a large freshwater cistern and a lighthouse. Reis Magos sits across the river from Panaji, Chapora overlooks the Chapora river in the north, and Cabo de Rama and Tiracol mark the southern and northern ends of the coast. Several began as forts of earlier rulers.

In Panaji, the Fontainhas quarter has narrow lanes of 19th-century houses with balcões (verandahs) and coloured walls. In the south, Chandor and Loutolim have large family houses, such as the Braganza House at Chandor, that show how landed families lived. Churches, cemeteries and wayside crosses across the villages are worth reading as public memory; our talk on [cemeteries, epitaphs and public memory](cemeteries-epitaphs-and-public-memory.html) gives groups a method.

sections.h2: Goa, spice and the Indian Ocean
paras: The Portuguese came to Goa for the trade in pepper, cinnamon and other goods of the Indian Ocean, and the crops they brought from the Americas, such as chillies, cashew and potato, changed Indian food for good. That makes Goa a good place to show students that heritage includes what we eat. Our session on [foods as historical evidence](foods-as-historical-evidence-coconut-spice-and-exchange.html) uses coconut, spice and exchange to tell this story.

For a wider look at architecture shared and borrowed across faiths, our lecture on [sacred architecture across communities](sacred-architecture-across-communities.html) compares church, temple and mosque plans, and fits a Goa trip well.

sections.h2: Planning a heritage visit to Goa for a group
paras: Old Goa, Panaji and the Ponda temples can be covered in one long day; Tambdi Surla, Usgalimal and the Arvalem caves need a second day inland. The monsoon is lush but heavy; the cooler months from November to February suit walking. Check the ASI or state archives and archaeology website before you go.

Each Goa trip is planned with the group. We plan [a study tour for your group](a-study-tour-built-for-your-group.html) and [private journeys](journeys.html) that take in all of Goa's layers, not only the churches.

faq.q: What is the UNESCO World Heritage Site in Goa?
faq.a: The Churches and Convents of Goa, inscribed in 1986. It covers the monuments of Old Goa, including the Basilica of Bom Jesus, the Se Cathedral, the Church of St Francis of Assisi, St Cajetan and the Chapel of St Catherine.

faq.q: Are there ancient temples in Goa?
faq.a: Yes. The Mahadeva temple at Tambdi Surla, of the Kadamba period, is the best preserved. The Arvalem caves are older rock-cut chambers. Many famous temples around Ponda were rebuilt in the 17th and 18th centuries after deities were moved inland.

faq.q: What are the Usgalimal rock carvings?
faq.a: They are more than a hundred engravings on laterite on the bank of the Kushavati river in south Goa, showing animals, people and a labyrinth pattern. They are usually considered prehistoric, though exact dates are uncertain.

faq.q: Can we book a heritage tour of Goa for students?
faq.a: Yes. Talaash Heritage designs custom study tours for schools and colleges in Goa on request, combining Old Goa with the Ponda temples, Tambdi Surla and Usgalimal, with a lecture before the trip.
